reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker or PD data reported to confirm sorafenib engaged VEGFR2/RAF1. The trial was designed to test whether sorafenib would enhance radiofrequency ablation coagulation zones, but no target engagement measurements were included. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers measured to assess whether kinase inhibition or angiogenesis inhibition occurred. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint clearly missed - coagulation zone volume was essentially identical between arms (30.7 vs 30.5 cm³, p=0.794). The hypothesis that sorafenib would enhance ablation zones through angiogenesis inhibition was not supported. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Small sample size (N=20) suggests underpowering. The endpoint itself is novel and its relationship to clinical benefit unclear. Safety signals included multiple SAEs in the sorafenib arm (leukopenia, lymphopenia, elevated liver enzymes) but these don't appear dose-limiting given the short 9-day treatment duration.
